issues.description: default_raise() and 'default_factory=default_raise' pattern is now obsolete with kw_only=True; remove the scaffolding.
issues.detail: default_raise() existed solely as a < 3.10 workaround so kw-only-like fields could appear without a real default. Now that all dataclasses use kw_only=True, fields with no sensible default should simply omit the default. Leaving default_factory=default_raise everywhere preserves a fossil that obscures the actual contract (required vs optional) and lets the RuntimeError trigger at runtime instead of TypeError at construction.

issues.description: Stale '< 3.10 compatibility' comment left after the workaround was removed.
issues.detail: The comment above TransactionEndpointRequest still reads 'this is for < 3.10 compatibility', referring to default_factory=default_raise. Since 3.9 is gone, the comment is now misleading literature: it tells the reader to preserve a constraint that no longer applies. Either delete the comment with the workaround or rewrite it to explain the current (kw-only required-field) intent.

issues.description: test-install-scripts.yml runs 'dnf search python3.12' in CI provisioning, which is diagnostic noise, not provisioning.
issues.detail: 'dnf search' prints matches but does not install or gate anything; if the package is missing, the following 'dnf install' fails anyway with a clearer error. Including search in the provisioning step adds log volume and a false sense of verification. Either drop the search line or replace it with an explicit 'dnf list installed python3.12' assertion after install.

issues.description: install.sh error message still says '>= 3.10 and < 3.13' but the version check uses PYTHON_MINOR_VER < 7.
issues.detail: The conditional reads '[ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -lt "7" ]' while the message claims the minimum is 3.10. A reader auditing the script will see the invariant 'minor >= 7' enforced and 'minor >= 10' announced — they disagree. Tighten the check to '-lt 10' so the code matches the message; otherwise Python 3.7/3.8/3.9 still pass the gate silently.

issues.description: Comment in conditions.py references a 3.9 coverage quirk that no longer applies; delete the historical note.
issues.detail: The removed pragma comment about 'something about python 3.9 makes this not covered' is gone, but similar archeological comments may remain elsewhere. The diff shows good hygiene here — recommend a grep pass for 'python 3.9', 'pragma: no cover.*3.9', 'pragma: no cover.*< 3.10' to find remaining stale literate notes that will mislead future readers.

review.summary: This PR is a mechanical version-floor bump: drop 3.9 from CI matrices, installers, and source-level compatibility shims, then collapse the kw_only conditionals into the unconditional 3.10+ form. The algorithmic content is essentially a substitution; there are no new invariants to audit and the one real semantic improvement (itertools.pairwise) is correct and idiomatic. Verdict: RIGOROUS on the core change, but NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT cleanup — the default_raise() scaffolding, stale '< 3.10' comments, and a mismatched minor-version check in install.sh are now fossils that lie to the reader. None block merge; all are cheap cleanups that pay readability interest forever.
